questions.stem: You create a OneLake shortcut in a lakehouse that points to a folder in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. What happens to the data?

options.text: It is copied into OneLake every hour
It stays in ADLS Gen2 and is read in place through the shortcut
It is copied into OneLake once, when the shortcut is created
It is moved into OneLake and removed from ADLS Gen2

questions.explanation: A shortcut is a reference: the data stays where it is, and Fabric engines read it through OneLake without copying or moving it.

questions.stem: A lakehouse has a shortcut to a folder in another workspace's lakehouse. You delete the shortcut. What happens to the folder it pointed to?

options.text: The folder and its files are deleted
Nothing: deleting a shortcut removes only the reference
The folder is moved into your lakehouse

questions.explanation: Deleting a shortcut deletes the shortcut object only. The target data is untouched.

questions.stem: Which three can a OneLake shortcut point to? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A table in a Fabric deployment pipeline
A folder in another Fabric lakehouse

questions.explanation: Shortcuts can point to other OneLake locations and to external storage such as ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3 and Google Cloud Storage. A report or a deployment pipeline isn't storage.

questions.stem: A folder in ADLS Gen2 holds a Delta table. You want it to appear as a table that Spark and the SQL analytics endpoint can query. Where do you create the shortcut?

options.text: In the workspace, outside any lakehouse
At the top level of the lakehouse's Tables section
In the lakehouse's Files section, in any subfolder

questions.explanation: A shortcut at the top level of Tables to a Delta folder is discovered as a table. A shortcut under Files appears as a folder of files.
